[Films](Film "Film") generate income from several revenue streams, including [theatrical exhibition](Movie_theater "Movie theater"), [home video](Home_video "Home video"), [television broadcast rights](Broadcasting_rights "Broadcasting rights"), and [merchandising](Merchandising "Merchandising"). However, theatrical [box-office](Box_office "Box office") earnings are the primary metric for trade publications in assessing the success of a film, mostly because of the availability of the data compared to sales figures for home video and broadcast rights, but also because of historical practice. Included on the list are charts of the top box-office earners (ranked by both the [nominal and real value](Real_versus_nominal_value_(economics) "Real versus nominal value (economics)") of their revenue), a chart of high-grossing films by calendar year, a timeline showing the transition of the highest-grossing film record, and a chart of the highest-grossing film franchises and series. All charts are ranked by international theatrical box-office performance where possible, excluding income derived from home video, broadcasting rights, and merchandise.

Traditionally, [war films](War_film "War film"), [musicals](Musical_film "Musical film"), and [historical dramas](List_of_historical_drama_films "List of historical drama films") have been the most popular genres, but [franchise films](Media_franchise "Media franchise") have been among the best performers of the 21st century. There is strong interest in the [superhero genre](Superhero_film "Superhero film"), with ten films in the [Marvel Cinematic Universe](Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") featuring among the nominal top-earners. The most successful superhero film, *[Avengers: Endgame](Avengers%3A_Endgame "Avengers: Endgame")*, is also the second-highest-grossing film on the nominal earnings chart, and there are four films in total based on the *[Avengers](Avengers_(comics) "Avengers (comics)")* comic books charting in the top twenty. Other [Marvel Comics adaptations](List_of_films_based_on_Marvel_Comics "List of films based on Marvel Comics") have also had success with the *[Spider-Man](Spider-Man_in_film "Spider-Man in film")* and *[X-Men](X-Men_(film_series) "X-Men (film series)")* properties, while films based on *[Batman](Batman_in_film "Batman in film")* and *[Superman](Superman_in_film "Superman in film")* from [DC Comics](DC_Comics "DC Comics") have generally performed well. *[Star Wars](Star_Wars "Star Wars")* is also represented in the nominal earnings chart with five films, while the *[Jurassic Park](Jurassic_Park "Jurassic Park")* franchise features prominently. Although the nominal earnings chart is dominated by films adapted from pre-existing properties and sequels, it is headed by *[Avatar](Avatar_(2009_film) "Avatar (2009 film)")*, which is an original work. Animated family films have performed consistently well, with [Disney films](List_of_Disney_theatrical_animated_features "List of Disney theatrical animated features") enjoying lucrative re-releases prior to the home-video era. Disney also enjoyed later success with films such as *[Frozen](Frozen_(2013_film) "Frozen (2013 film)")* and *[Frozen II](Frozen_II "Frozen II")*, *<Zootopia>*, and *[The Lion King](The_Lion_King "The Lion King")* (with [its computer-animated remake](The_Lion_King_(2019_film) "The Lion King (2019 film)") as the [highest-grossing animated film](List_of_highest-grossing_animated_films "List of highest-grossing animated films")), as well as its [Pixar](List_of_Pixar_films "List of Pixar films") brand, of which *[Incredibles 2](Incredibles_2 "Incredibles 2")*, *[Toy Story 3](Toy_Story_3 "Toy Story 3")* and *[4](Toy_Story_4 "Toy Story 4")*, and *[Finding Dory](Finding_Dory "Finding Dory")* have been the best performers. Beyond Disney and Pixar animation, the *[Despicable Me](Despicable_Me "Despicable Me")*, *[Shrek](Shrek_(franchise) "Shrek (franchise)")*, and *[Ice Age](Ice_Age_(franchise) "Ice Age (franchise)")* series have met with the most success.

While [inflation](Inflation "Inflation") has eroded the achievements of most films from the 1950s, 1960s, and 1970s, there are franchises originating from that period that are still active. Besides the *Star Wars* and *Superman* franchises, *[James Bond](James_Bond_in_film "James Bond in film")* and *[Godzilla](Godzilla_(franchise) "Godzilla (franchise)")* films are still being released periodically; all four are among the highest-grossing franchises. Some of the older films that held the record of highest-grossing film still have respectable grosses by today's standards, but no longer compete numerically against today's top-earners in an era of much higher individual ticket prices. content:
Based on my research from Wikipedia, here are the directors of the five highest-grossing films of 2023:

| Rank | Film | Director(s) | Worldwide Gross |
|------|------|-------------|-----------------|
| 1 | **Barbie** | Greta Gerwig | $1,417,722,143 |
| 2 | **The Super Mario Bros. Movie** | Aaron Horvath & Michael Jelenic | $1,360,454,146 |
| 3 | **Oppenheimer** | Christopher Nolan | $912,739,000 |
| 4 | **Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3** | James Gunn | $845,555,777 |
| 5 | **Fast X** | Louis Leterrier | $714,520,077 |

Notable points:
- **Greta Gerwig** made history with "Barbie" as the highest-grossing movie ever with a solo female director
- **The Super Mario Bros. Movie** had two directors (Aaron Horvath and Michael Jelenic)
- **Christopher Nolan** won critical acclaim for "Oppenheimer," an R-rated biographical thriller
- **James Gunn** directed his final installment in the Guardians trilogy before taking over DC Studios
- **Louis Leterrier** took over directing duties for "Fast X" (the franchise later moved to Justin Lin for the next film)
